Show SVM full CV, selection, refit and export code 
# Original standalone entry point runs from SVM_week12/ after its shared preprocessing.
# Source: SVM_week12/svm_model.R
svm_run_cv <- function(cv_data, cv_folds, x_train, y_train,
                       output_dir = "svm_results") {
  stopifnot(length(cv_data) == 5L, length(cv_folds) == 5L,
            nrow(x_train) == length(y_train), !anyNA(x_train), !anyNA(y_train))
  classes <- levels(y_train)
  stopifnot(length(classes) == 5L,
            identical(sort(as.integer(unlist(cv_folds))), seq_along(y_train)))
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  # Baseline = C=1, gamma=1/p, no class weights. It is one grid candidate.
  grid <- expand.grid(C = c(0.1, 1, 10), Gamma_multiplier = c(0.25, 1, 4),
                       Weighting = c("none", "inverse"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  grid$Candidate <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
  baseline_id <- grid$Candidate[grid$C == 1 & grid$Gamma_multiplier == 1 &
                                grid$Weighting == "none"]
  prepared <- lapply(seq_along(cv_data), function(k) {
    fold <- cv_data[[k]]
    stopifnot(identical(as.character(fold$y_valid),
                        as.character(y_train[cv_folds[[k]]])),
              nrow(fold$x_train) + nrow(fold$x_valid) == length(y_train),
              all(table(fold$y_train) > 0), all(table(fold$y_valid) > 0))
    encoder <- svm_fit_encoder(fold$x_train)
    list(x_train = svm_apply_encoder(encoder, fold$x_train),
         x_valid = svm_apply_encoder(encoder, fold$x_valid),
         y_train = fold$y_train, y_valid = fold$y_valid,
         encoder = encoder)
  })
  # Independent parameter candidates can run in local R worker processes.
  # Default is sequential, so sourcing this file also works in ordinary RStudio.
  workers <- max(1L, min(3L, as.integer(getOption("stat5003.svm.workers", 1L))))
  cache_dir <- file.path(output_dir, "candidate_cache")
  dir.create(cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  fingerprint <- digest::digest(list(cv_data, cv_folds, grid, "svm-v1"))
  run_candidate <- function(i) {
    cache_file <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0(fingerprint, "_", i, ".rds"))
    if (file.exists(cache_file)) return(readRDS(cache_file))
    candidate <- grid[i, ]
    scores <- vector("list", length(prepared))
    fold_predictions <- vector("list", length(prepared))
    for (k in seq_along(prepared)) {
      fold <- prepared[[k]]
      t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
      model <- svm_train(fold$x_train, fold$y_train, candidate$C,
                         candidate$Gamma_multiplier, candidate$Weighting)
      pred <- predict(model, fold$x_valid)
      metric <- svm_metrics(fold$y_valid, pred, classes)$summary
      scores[[k]] <- cbind(
        candidate, Fold = k, Gamma = candidate$Gamma_multiplier / ncol(fold$x_train),
        Encoded_predictors = ncol(fold$x_train), metric,
        Support_vectors = model$tot.nSV,
        Seconds = proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0
      )
      fold_predictions[[k]] <- data.frame(
        Row = cv_folds[[k]], Fold = k, Actual = as.character(fold$y_valid),
        Predicted = as.character(pred), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      progress <- sprintf("SVM %02d/%02d fold %d/5: C=%g gamma=%g/%d %s; macro-F1=%.4f (%.1fs)",
                      i, nrow(grid), k, candidate$C, candidate$Gamma_multiplier,
                      ncol(fold$x_train), candidate$Weighting, metric$Macro_F1,
                      proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0)
      message(progress)
      cat(progress, "\n", file = file.path(cache_dir, paste0("progress_", i, ".txt")), append = TRUE)
    }
    result <- list(scores = do.call(rbind, scores), predictions = do.call(rbind, fold_predictions))
    saveRDS(result, cache_file)
    result
  }
  if (workers > 1L) {
    cluster <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(workers)
    on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cluster), add = TRUE)
    parallel::clusterCall(cluster, function(paths) .libPaths(paths), .libPaths())
    # Worker tasks fit and score only the prepared training/CV partitions.
    parallel::clusterExport(cluster, c("svm_train", "svm_class_weights", "svm_metrics"),
                             envir = environment(svm_train))
    candidate_results <- parallel::parLapplyLB(cluster, seq_len(nrow(grid)), run_candidate)
  } else {
    candidate_results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), run_candidate)
  }
  predictions <- lapply(candidate_results, `[[`, "predictions")
  fold_scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(candidate_results, `[[`, "scores"))
  write.csv(fold_scores, file.path(output_dir, "cv_fold_scores.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  tuning <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
    z <- fold_scores[fold_scores$Candidate == i, ]
    cbind(grid[i, ], Mean_Macro_F1 = mean(z$Macro_F1), SD_Macro_F1 = sd(z$Macro_F1),
          Mean_Balanced_Accuracy = mean(z$Balanced_Accuracy),
          Mean_Accuracy = mean(z$Accuracy), Total_seconds = sum(z$Seconds))
  }))
  tuning <- tuning[order(-tuning$Mean_Macro_F1, tuning$SD_Macro_F1,
                         tuning$C, tuning$Gamma_multiplier, tuning$Weighting), ]
  rownames(tuning) <- NULL
  best <- tuning[1, ]
  baseline <- tuning[tuning$Candidate == baseline_id, ]
  selected_oof <- predictions[[best$Candidate]]
  selected_oof <- selected_oof[order(selected_oof$Row), ]
  baseline_oof <- predictions[[baseline_id]]
  baseline_oof <- baseline_oof[order(baseline_oof$Row), ]
  stopifnot(identical(as.integer(selected_oof$Row), seq_along(y_train)),
            identical(as.character(y_train), selected_oof$Actual))
  oof_metrics <- svm_metrics(selected_oof$Actual, selected_oof$Predicted, classes)
  best_weighted <- tuning[tuning$Weighting == "inverse", ][1, ]
  weighted_oof <- predictions[[best_weighted$Candidate]]
  weighted_metrics <- svm_metrics(weighted_oof$Actual, weighted_oof$Predicted, classes)
  weighting_tradeoff <- rbind(
    cbind(Variant = "Selected by macro-F1", oof_metrics$per_class),
    cbind(Variant = "Best weighted SVM", weighted_metrics$per_class))
  # One stable comparison row per variant for the group-wide model table.
  comparison <- rbind(cbind(Model = "SVM baseline", baseline),
                       cbind(Model = "SVM selected by CV", best))
  encoder <- svm_fit_encoder(x_train)
  final_model <- svm_train(svm_apply_encoder(encoder, x_train), y_train,
                           best$C, best$Gamma_multiplier, best$Weighting)
  bundle <- list(model = final_model, encoder = encoder, best = best,
                  class_levels = classes,
                  note = "Training-only refit. Holdout has NOT been evaluated.")
  write.csv(tuning, file.path(output_dir, "tuning_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(comparison, file.path(output_dir, "baseline_vs_selected.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(selected_oof, file.path(output_dir, "selected_oof_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(baseline_oof, file.path(output_dir, "baseline_oof_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(oof_metrics$per_class, file.path(output_dir, "oof_per_class.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(best_weighted, file.path(output_dir, "best_weighted_cv.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(weighting_tradeoff, file.path(output_dir, "weighting_tradeoff.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(oof_metrics$summary, file.path(output_dir, "oof_pooled_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(as.data.frame.matrix(oof_metrics$confusion),
            file.path(output_dir, "oof_confusion_matrix.csv"))
  saveRDS(bundle, file.path(output_dir, "svm_training_refit.rds"))
  capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_dir, "sessionInfo.txt"))
  writeLines(c(
    "Balanced_Accuracy is macro-averaged class recall (mean sensitivity), not mean one-vs-rest (sensitivity+specificity)/2.",
    "Mean_Macro_F1 is the unweighted mean of the five fold macro-F1 values; SD is their sample standard deviation.",
    "Pooled OOF metrics pool all held-out fold predictions and need not equal the fold means.",
    "The selected configuration maximises mean CV macro-F1 across 18 candidates (90 fits).",
    "The same CV folds were used for tuning and reporting; selected CV scores are optimistic development estimates, not an independent final performance estimate.",
    "No x_test or y_test was used in tuning, selection or model fitting. Only score the holdout after the group selects its final model.",
    "The final saved SVM was refit using full training data; its encoder and class weights were learned again from full training only."
  ), file.path(output_dir, "metric_definitions.txt"))
  list(tuning = tuning, fold_scores = fold_scores, comparison = comparison,
       selected_oof = selected_oof, baseline_oof = baseline_oof,
       oof = oof_metrics, bundle = bundle,
       best_weighted = best_weighted, weighting_tradeoff = weighting_tradeoff)
}

svm_plot_results <- function(result, output_dir = "svm_results") {
  if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) return(invisible(NULL))
  tuning_plot <- result$tuning
  tuning_plot$Text_colour <- ifelse(
    tuning_plot$Mean_Macro_F1 > mean(range(tuning_plot$Mean_Macro_F1)), "white", "#17324d")
  p_tuning <- ggplot2::ggplot(tuning_plot, ggplot2::aes(
    x = factor(C), y = factor(Gamma_multiplier), fill = Mean_Macro_F1)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", Mean_Macro_F1), colour = Text_colour), size = 5) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_identity() +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ Weighting) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e8f3fa", high = "#12648a") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "SVM tuning: mean macro-F1 across shared five-fold CV",
                   x = "Cost (C)", y = "Gamma multiplier (gamma = multiplier / p)", fill = "Macro-F1") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(14, 18, 14, 14),
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13))
  cm <- as.data.frame(result$oof$confusion)
  cm$Within_actual <- cm$Freq / rowSums(result$oof$confusion)[match(cm$Actual, rownames(result$oof$confusion))]
  cm$Text_colour <- ifelse(cm$Within_actual > 0.5, "white", "#17324d")
  p_cm <- ggplot2::ggplot(cm, ggplot2::aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Within_actual)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%d\n%.1f%%", Freq, 100 * Within_actual), colour = Text_colour), size = 3.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_identity() +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(result$oof$per_class$Class)) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eef4f8", high = "#12648a", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Selected SVM: cross-validation confusion matrix",
                   subtitle = "Out-of-fold predictions; same folds used for tuning",
                   fill = "Row share") + ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(14, 18, 14, 14),
                    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 13),
                    plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10))
  p_recall <- ggplot2::ggplot(result$oof$per_class, ggplot2::aes(x = Class, y = Recall)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#12648a", width = 0.65) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * Recall)), vjust = -0.4) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.05), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2),
                               labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")) +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Which outcomes does SVM identify?", x = NULL, y = "Out-of-fold recall") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "svm_tuning.png"), p_tuning, width = 9, height = 4.5, dpi = 160)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "svm_confusion_matrix.png"), p_cm, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 160)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "svm_recall.png"), p_recall, width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 160)
  invisible(list(tuning = p_tuning, confusion = p_cm, recall = p_recall))
}

# Run this after the group's common-cv-preprocessing chunk.
svm_results <- svm_run_cv(cv_data, cv_folds, x_train, y_train)
svm_plot_results(svm_results)
print(svm_results$comparison)
print(svm_results$oof$per_class)

XGBoost

For configurations B and C, each training row receives the weight n / (K × nc) (training rows n, classes K = 5, rows in the row’s class nc), passed to xgb.DMatrix. Every class then carries the same total weight, n / K, in the training loss. Weights are computed from the training rows of each fold (and from the full training set for the final model) only.

Four hyperparameters are tuned by grid search: tree depth (max_depth: 4, 6), learning rate (eta: 0.05, 0.10), the fraction of columns sampled per tree (colsample_bytree: 0.70, 0.85) and the minimum child weight (min_child_weight: 1, 3). These control model complexity and the degree of regularisation of the boosted trees (Chen & Guestrin, 2016). For the tuned configurations, the row sampling fraction (subsample) is fixed at 0.80 and the number of boosting rounds at 150. Each of the 16 configurations is evaluated on the five shared folds in cv_data, and the one with the highest mean macro-F1 is selected. To separate the effect of the weights from the effect of tuning, the results below compare three configurations on the same folds: (A) library defaults without weights, (B) library defaults with balanced weights, and (C) the tuned configuration with balanced weights.

Show XGBoost results-table code 
xgb_display <- xgb_cv
xgb_display$Configuration <- c("A. Unweighted model baseline", "B. Baseline + balanced weights", "C. Tuned + balanced weights")
knitr::kable(xgb_display[, c("Configuration", "Mean_CV_Macro_F1", "SD_CV_Macro_F1", "Mean_CV_Balanced_Accuracy", "Mean_CV_Accuracy")],
             digits = 3, col.names = c("Configuration", "Macro-F1", "Fold SD", "Balanced accuracy", "Accuracy"),
             caption = "Table 4. XGBoost weighting and tuning on identical folds and 150-round budgets.")
Table 4. XGBoost weighting and tuning on identical folds and 150-round budgets.
Configuration Macro-F1 Fold SD Balanced accuracy Accuracy
A. Unweighted model baseline 0.489 0.016 0.468 0.794
B. Baseline + balanced weights 0.476 0.012 0.515 0.693
C. Tuned + balanced weights 0.492 0.013 0.553 0.685

The selected configuration (max_depth = 6, eta = 0.05, colsample_bytree = 0.85, min_child_weight = 3) reached a mean macro-F1 of 0.492 (SD 0.013). Adding balanced weights changed mean macro-F1 from 0.489 (A) to 0.476 (B), and mean accuracy from 0.794 to 0.693. Tuning changed mean macro-F1 from 0.476 (B) to 0.492 (C). Because the selected value is the maximum over 16 candidates, it is the selection criterion and not an independent performance estimate; the held-out result in Section 8 is reported separately.

Show XGBoost weighting, grid search and export code 
# Source: model_comparison/run_xgb_review.R
B <- fit_config(default_params, TRUE, "B. Defaults, balanced weights")
message("Completed B: weighted defaults")

tuning_grid <- expand.grid(max_depth = c(4L, 6L), eta = c(0.05, 0.10), subsample = 0.80,
                           colsample_bytree = c(0.70, 0.85), min_child_weight = c(1, 3),
                           KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
grid_fits <- vector("list", nrow(tuning_grid))
grid_summaries <- vector("list", nrow(tuning_grid))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tuning_grid))) {
  grid_fits[[i]] <- fit_config(as.list(tuning_grid[i, ]), TRUE,
                              "C. Tuned, balanced weights", i)
  grid_summaries[[i]] <- cbind(data.frame(Grid_ID = i), tuning_grid[i, ],
                              summarise_folds(grid_fits[[i]]$folds))
  message(sprintf("Completed configuration %d/%d", i, nrow(tuning_grid)))
}
grid_summary <- do.call(rbind, grid_summaries)
# The first configuration is retained if mean macro-F1 ties, matching the source analysis.
best_index <- which.max(grid_summary$Mean_CV_Macro_F1)
best_params <- as.list(tuning_grid[best_index, ])
C <- grid_fits[[best_index]]
configuration_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(list(A, B, C), function(x) {
  cbind(data.frame(Configuration = x$folds$Configuration[1L]), summarise_folds(x$folds))
}))
write_result(configuration_summary, "xgb_configuration_summary.csv")
write_result(rbind(A$folds, B$folds, C$folds), "xgb_configuration_fold_scores.csv")
write_result(do.call(rbind, lapply(grid_fits, `[[`, "folds")), "xgb_grid_fold_scores.csv")
write_result(grid_summary, "xgb_grid_summary.csv")
write_result(C$folds, "xgb_selected_oof_fold_scores.csv")
write_result(data.frame(Training_Row = seq_along(y_train), Actual = as.character(y_train),
                         Predicted = as.character(C$predictions)), "xgb_selected_oof_predictions.csv")
write_result(class_metrics(y_train, C$predictions), "xgb_oof_per_class.csv")
write_result(confusion_table(y_train, C$predictions), "xgb_oof_confusion_matrix.csv")
selected <- cbind(data.frame(Model = "XGBoost", nrounds = xgb_nrounds, seed = xgb_seed),
                  tuning_grid[best_index, ], summarise_folds(C$folds),
                  score_predictions(y_train, C$predictions))
write_result(selected, "xgb_selected_metrics.csv")

7. Model Evaluation & Selection

Evaluation metrics

For class c, precision = TP/(TP + FP), recall = TP/(TP + FN), and F1 = 2TP/(2TP + FP + FN), using that class’s true positives, false positives and false negatives. Precision and F1 are defined as zero when a class is never predicted. Macro-F1 is the unweighted mean of the five class F1 scores and is the primary selection measure. Balanced accuracy is mean class recall; overall accuracy is secondary. Weighted-F1 weights each class F1 by prevalence and can conceal poor minority-class performance.

Cross-validated comparison

Table 5 reports the mean of the five fold scores and the SD of macro-F1. Figure 5 pools one out-of-fold prediction per training animal for class-specific recall. All models use the same animal assignments, target labels and folds. The folds are also used for tuning, so these are selection results, not unbiased estimates from nested cross-validation. Fold SD describes variation across these folds; it is not a confidence interval.

Show R code 
comparison_display <- comparison %>% transmute(Model,
  `Macro-F1 (mean ± SD)` = sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", Macro_F1, SD),
  `Balanced accuracy` = fmt(Balanced_Accuracy), Accuracy = fmt(Accuracy))
knitr::kable(comparison_display, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"), caption = "Table 5. Shared five-fold validation; macro-F1 is the selection criterion.")
Table 5. Shared five-fold validation; macro-F1 is the selection criterion.
Model Macro-F1 (mean ± SD) Balanced accuracy Accuracy
XGBoost 0.492 ± 0.013 0.553 0.685
Random forest 0.484 ± 0.016 0.462 0.800
RBF SVM 0.456 ± 0.012 0.440 0.800
Multinomial logistic (M3) 0.441 ± 0.012 0.521 0.624
Majority class (baseline) 0.138 ± 0.000 0.200 0.524
Show R code 
ggplot(recall_long, aes(Class, Recall, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#3578A3", "#5A9975", "#B98342", "#8270A1")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Recall", fill = NULL,
       caption = "Figure 5. Pooled out-of-fold recall for all four models; each animal is predicted outside its training fold.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

XGBoost is selected among the four completed models. Its mean macro-F1 of 0.492 exceeds random forest by 0.008; this small difference is not evidence of a decisive advantage. The practical distinction is its greater recall for Euthanasia and Other. Random forest and SVM achieve about 0.80 accuracy but identify few Euthanasia cases. Logistic M3 has lower macro-F1, although its stronger Return and Other recall makes it informative when missed cases are a priority.

XGBoost’s lower accuracy (0.685) is a trade-off: improved attention to rare outcomes comes with more errors among common outcomes. Macro-F1 balances class precision and recall but does not encode a shelter’s actual error costs. Staff would need to determine those costs before adopting a model or decision threshold.

8. Final Results & Conclusion

Held-out assessment

After CV selection, the chosen XGBoost configuration is refitted on all 13,467 training animals for the same 150 rounds and evaluated on the 3,364 test animals. Test labels do not determine parameters or the number of rounds in this procedure. Earlier project versions had already reported results on this split; this is a reproduced assessment, not a newly blinded test.

Show final XGBoost refit, test predictions and importance code 
# Source: model_comparison/run_xgb_review.R
# Holdout is scored after hyperparameter selection. It never determines parameters/rounds.
full <- make_matrices(x_train, y_train, x_test, y_test)
final_model <- xgb.train(params = c(base_params, best_params), data = full$weighted,
                         nrounds = xgb_nrounds, verbose = 0)
holdout_pred <- predict_classes(final_model, full$valid, length(y_test))
write_result(cbind(data.frame(Model = "XGBoost", nrounds = xgb_nrounds),
                    score_predictions(y_test, holdout_pred)), "xgb_holdout_metrics.csv")
write_result(class_metrics(y_test, holdout_pred), "xgb_holdout_per_class.csv")
write_result(confusion_table(y_test, holdout_pred), "xgb_holdout_confusion_matrix.csv")
write_result(data.frame(Test_Row = seq_along(y_test), Actual = as.character(y_test),
                         Predicted = as.character(holdout_pred)), "xgb_holdout_predictions.csv")
majority <- names(which.max(table(y_train)))
write_result(cbind(data.frame(Model = "Majority class", Majority_Class = majority),
                    score_predictions(y_test, rep(majority, length(y_test)))), "majority_holdout_metrics.csv")
write_result(cbind(data.frame(Majority_Class = majority),
                    score_predictions(y_train, rep(majority, length(y_train)))), "majority_training_metrics.csv")

importance <- xgb.importance(feature_names = full$feature_names, model = final_model)
importance_by_predictor <- data.frame(
  Predictor = model_predictors,
  Gain = vapply(model_predictors, function(p) {
    sum(importance$Gain[importance$Feature == p | startsWith(importance$Feature, paste0(p, "."))])
  }, numeric(1)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
importance_by_predictor <- importance_by_predictor[order(-importance_by_predictor$Gain), ]
stopifnot(abs(sum(importance_by_predictor$Gain) - 1) < 1e-5)
write_result(importance_by_predictor, "xgb_feature_importance.csv")
write_result(as.data.frame(importance), "xgb_encoded_feature_importance.csv")
write_result(data.frame(Class = outcome_levels, Training = as.integer(table(y_train)),
                         Holdout = as.integer(table(y_test))), "split_class_counts.csv")
writeLines(c(
  "XGBoost: fixed 150 boosting rounds for all A/B/C configurations and final refit.",
  "Seed 5003, nthread 2, common five stratified folds; training-only preprocessing and weights.",
  "A: defaults, unweighted; B: defaults, balanced weights; C: balanced weights plus 16-point grid.",
  "Select highest mean fold macro-F1; tie selects first grid row. No early stopping.",
  "Ranking, per-class metrics and confusion matrices reuse the selected grid's OOF predictions.",
  "The holdout does not determine parameters, rounds or model choice.",
  "This reproduces the latest branch analysis; prior project versions already inspected the holdout.",
  paste("R", getRversion(), "; xgboost", utils::packageVersion("xgboost")),
  paste("Source dataset MD5:", unname(tools::md5sum("Austin_Animal_Center_Outcomes_20260916.csv")))
), file.path(output_dir, "xgb_protocol.txt"))
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(output_dir, "sessionInfo.txt"))

test_predictions <- read_result("xgb_holdout_predictions.csv")
confusion <- as.data.frame(table(Actual = factor(test_predictions$Actual, levels = classes),
                                Predicted = factor(test_predictions$Predicted, levels = classes))) %>%
  group_by(Actual) %>% mutate(Share = Freq / sum(Freq))

  geom_tile(colour = "white") + geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 3.2) +

Held-out macro-F1 is 0.478, compared with 0.492 in CV and 0.138 for the majority rule. Euthanasia recall is 28.9% and precision is 16.7%: many actual cases are missed, and many predictions of this outcome are false positives. The model therefore cannot determine an individual animal’s care or disposition.

Interpretation and process reflection

Aggregating split gain over one-hot columns identifies Spayed.Neutered (37.0% of total gain) and Age_Years_imputed (31.7%) as the two largest contributors. Gain describes how the fitted trees split this dataset. Correlated predictors can share importance, and these values neither establish causation nor show that a field was available at intake.

Show R code

The Data Investigation Process connected the audit to implementation: repeated identifiers led to one record per animal, sparse breeds to training-based grouping, and imbalance to macro-F1 and per-class error analysis. Comparing unweighted, weighted and tuned models showed why a plausible adjustment does not necessarily improve the chosen metric. Shared folds allowed a consistent comparison; a stronger evaluation would fix the complete protocol before examining assessment results and reserve a later period for testing.

Answer to the research question and limitations

Recorded animal characteristics provide useful but incomplete information about shelter outcomes. Among the four completed classifiers, tuned weighted XGBoost has the highest mean CV macro-F1. Its held-out macro-F1 is 0.478. Its small advantage over random forest and its lower overall accuracy make the choice dependent on the importance of recognising less common outcomes. The results support further evaluation as an aid to staff review, rather than automated outcome decisions.

The largest practical concern is prediction-time availability. In the logistic sensitivity analysis, excluding spay/neuter status reduces mean CV macro-F1 from 0.441 to 0.369; excluding both that field and name reduces it to 0.362. This dependence does not prove leakage, but it makes verification of intake-time values essential. The same sensitivity checks have not been established for XGBoost.

Other limitations are the heterogeneous Other class, EDA conducted before the split, tuning and ranking on the same folds, and a target population restricted to the latest recorded admission per animal. A random split from one shelter does not establish performance in later periods or other shelters. Future work should verify field timestamps, evaluate a later admission cohort, and assess calibration and stakeholder-defined error costs before operational use.

Reproducibility

Figures are embedded in this HTML and all source panels are collapsed by default. Sections 4–8 show preprocessing, model fitting, tuning, prediction, evaluation and export code alongside the results they support. The accompanying source package retains the complete model files and data. The commands below regenerate each model’s outputs, verify the results and render the report; they are not run during ordinary report rendering. R session information is included for SVM and the XGBoost run; reruns under other package versions can differ numerically.
